decision_conditions: <p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-size:11pt">1.&nbsp;The proposal fails to demonstrate that it would address&nbsp;an identified need for childcare within the area, in the absence of a sufficient Needs Assessment.&nbsp;The proposed development would result in the loss of a family-sized dwellinghouse, the need for which is clearly demonstrated in the development plan and supporting evidence base.&nbsp;The provision of a new childcare facility in this location is therefore at odds with the following policies which seek to ensure that proposals for new social infrastructure meet an identified need and are appropriately located:</span></p><ul><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">National Planning Policy Framework (December 2023) </span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">Policies GG1, S1, and S3 of the London Plan (March 2021) </span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">Policies SP3, CM1,&nbsp;and SP4&nbsp;of&nbsp;The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan: (September 2024)</span></li></ul>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed development&nbsp;would result in unneighbourly levels of noise generation, increased comings-and-goings and general disturbances to neighbouring dwellings, to the extent that this would constitute undue harm to the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers. The proposal is therefore found to be at odds with the following policies which seek to ensure that development proposals adequately protect residential amenity: </span></p><ul><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">National Planning Policy Framework (December 2023) </span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">Policies GG3, D6 (part D) and D14 of the London Plan (March 2021) </span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">Policies DMD1 and DMSI3 of&nbsp;The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan: (September 2024)</span></li></ul>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed development is not&nbsp;sustainably located with a range of travel options, failing to support sustainable modes of transport and provide adequate cycle storage. In the absence of further information, it is likely that the proposal would result in increased comings-and-goings by car, resulting in increased vehicular movements and parking pressure within the surrounding area. As such, the development is contrary to:&nbsp;</span></p><ul><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">National Planning Policy Framework (December 2023)</span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">Policies T1, T2, T4, T5 and T6 of the London Plan (March 2021)</span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">Policies SP8, DMT1, DMT3 and DMT2 of&nbsp;The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan: (September 2024)</span></li></ul>

<div>The scale, siting and design of the proposed rear extension would result in the introduction of significant bulk, mass and scale to the rear of the site, creating an intense sense of overbearing and significantly impacting the adjoining neighbour, and character of the area. The proposed rear extension therefore constitutes unneighbourly development and contrary to:<br></div><div><br></div><div><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
